sections.content:
Population change in Bournemouth

The population in Bournemouth is projected to increase from 194,355 in 2018 to 196,803 people in 2028.

The biggest factor in population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 7,494.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Bournemouth
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Office for National Statistics – Subnational population projections for England.

sections.content:
In Bournemouth, this is how all the different factors are projected to contribute to population change between 2018 and 2028:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 0.7% (1,269), compared with an increase of 1.6% in England, with 18,032 births and 19,301 deaths in Bournemouth between 2018 and 2028.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in England) is projected to reduce the population by 1.4% (2,750), with 169,668 people entering the area and 172,418 people leaving the area between 2018 and 2028.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 0.4% (860), with 3,886 people entering the area and 4,746 people leaving the area between 2018 and 2028.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 3.9% (7,494), compared with an increase of 3.5% in England, with 30,963 people entering the area and 23,469 people leaving the area between 2018 and 2028.

sections.content:
Age profile in Bournemouth in 2028

The median age in Bournemouth is projected to rise from 38 years in 2018 to 40 years in 2028.

In England, the median age is projected to be 40 years in 2028.

Between 2018 and 2028, the proportion of people aged 65 years or over in Bournemouth is projected to rise from 18% to 20%.

sections.title: The 10 to 19 age group are set to see the largest increases in Bournemouth over the next 10 years.
sections.subtitle: Proportion of population by 10 year age bands, 2018 and 2028
sections.source: Office for National Statistics – Subnational population projections for England.

sections.content:
Between 2018 and 2028, the working population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Bournemouth is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of pensionable age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 283 to 324 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2028 (319 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Bournemouth?

Between 2018 and 2028, the number of people aged 18 years and under in Bournemouth is projected to stay the same, at around 20%.

This is below average for England in 2028 (23%).
